escalation-policy: Escalation policy. Escalate an unresolved ticket to tier 2 when it is older than 3 days and has never been escalated. A ticket may be escalated only once; after that, reassign it instead. Always record a one-line reason.
reassignment: Reassigning tickets. Reassign a ticket when its current agent is unavailable or the ticket was already escalated once. Pick the agent with the fewest open tickets.
closing-criteria: Closing tickets. Close a ticket only after the customer confirms the fix, or after 7 days without a customer reply. Never close an escalated ticket yourself.
sla-targets: Service level targets. First response within 1 day. Resolution within 5 days for normal tickets and within 2 days for urgent tickets.
security-incidents: Security incidents. If a ticket mentions leaked credentials or unauthorized access, do not reply to the customer. Page the security on-call immediately.
refunds: Refunds. Support agents may approve refunds up to 2000 rupees. Larger refunds go to the billing team with the ticket id and order number.
priority-levels: Priority levels. A ticket is urgent if the customer cannot use the product at all, or if payments are affected. Every other ticket is normal priority.
data-requests: Personal data requests. If a customer asks for a copy of their personal data, or asks for their account to be deleted, forward the ticket to the privacy team within 1 day.
